lessons.title: Pancreatic necrosis with a changing infection picture
tags: later suspected infected necrosis with deterioration
lessons.opening: On day five of pancreatitis, a 48-year-old has intermittent fever but improving pain and stable organs. CT shows necrosis without gas and infection is not established. Give a one-sentence problem representation.
reveals: At this first decision point, cultures do not establish infection and improvement continues. Antibiotics are requested solely because necrosis exists.
One week later the simulated course changes: hypotension, gram-negative bacteremia and gas in a pancreatic collection are documented. This is a new decision point.
Family heard intervention should wait four weeks and asks whether that means no action during deterioration. Specialist source-control review is being arranged.
facts: Sterile necrosis alone is not an indication for prophylactic antibiotics; infected necrosis and deterioration require a different treatment/source-control assessment.
